chronology: FRAME: Tonto and Lothar, two robots aboard the metabunker spacecraft, open a storytelling exchange; Lothar demands the origin story of the Metabaron caste and Tonto reluctantly agrees.
BACKSTORY BEGINS: Tonto identifies Othon von Salza, a former intergalactic pirate, as the Metabaron's great-great-grandfather.
Othon wins Lady Edna's hand; Edna is the daughter of Baron Berard, undisputed ruler of Marmola and Castaka in the Philorian system; they produce one son, Bari.
An Imperial Merchants Guild cargo ship arrives at Marmola on behalf of the Techno-Pope, who requires vast quantities of marble for a new temple-bank.

The ship's crew observe that the Marmolans cut stone manually with hyperlaser tools and load cargo by a secret method: after a feasting ritual the visitors wake from drunkenness to find the hold already full.
Baron Berard's team (including Edna, Bari, Hohenhole, and Sire Barako) performs a precision marble-cutting operation under the observation of imperial visitors.
Othon ignores his father-in-law's timing instructions and triggers a premature cutting discharge; a massive stone block falls and traps him beneath the rubble.
Elders debate whether to use their secret resource to save Othon, warning that exposure to the imperial visitors would end galactic peace.
The council votes to save Othon, overruling the elder patriarch; a figure uses a small glowing orb to levitate the stone block; the operator collapses from the effort.
An imperial authority witnessing the event declares it the greatest technical revolution of the century.

Baron Berard orders the visitors killed and commands that they be given their marble; he decrees Othon will become the new baron and must swear loyalty to the Empire, rebuking Othon for thinking like a pirate.
Baron Berard initiates a duel against Othon using a short dagger revered as an ancient Terra Prima weapon; Berard wins, having deliberately accepted a shoulder wound as a strategic sacrifice.
Berard explains to Othon that victory requires the willingness to sacrifice; he formally accepts Othon as his worthy heir and his daughter's chosen mate.
Berard performs a spirit and birthmark transfer, passing his lineage mark and knowledge into Othon, then bids farewell and prepares to die.
Berard dies after predicting that wars of conquest over the planet's sacred oil will erupt across the galaxy; he instructs his body be cast into the Great Azure Ocean.
Ten days after Berard's death, ships from multiple armed factions converge on Marmola and a massive space battle erupts.
The Imperial House deploys gigantic battleships and crushes the rival fleets; the Black Endoguard delivers an unexpected betrayal that proves decisive.
Imperial forces besiege the Castaka fortress; roughly 150 traditional defenders face approximately 1,500 heavily armed attackers.
The defenders reject a surrender offer on grounds of honor and warrior oath; close-quarters melee erupts in the fortress hall.
A warrior of Castaka cuts through multiple guards in a stairwell and crashes through a window; the volume ends at a cliffhanger with the next episode titled 'The Last Stand.'
locations: The metabunker — an impregnable fortress within a bustling city-shaft; setting for the robot framing narrative; contains a large faceted object suspended in a glowing sphere at its heart.
Marmola — a gigantic marble-producing world in the Philorian system; almost entirely stone with one small fertile valley; primary setting of the volume's flashback.

Castaka — the fortress-valley on Marmola and seat of Baron Berard's rule; also described as a wealthy imperial center and 'planet of gold,' suggesting the name covers both the local fortress and a broader domain.
Space above Marmola — site of the multi-faction space battle that erupts ten days after Berard's death.
The Great Azure Ocean — a named body of water designated by Berard for his funerary disposal.
The Castaka fortress hall — interior site of the final siege and last-stand melee at the volume's cliffhanger ending.
lore_laws: Meta-warrior initiation is hereditary: the father deliberately destroys the son's right ear and part of the right brain, which are then replaced with bionic components.
The Metabaron lineage is transmitted through a spirit and birthmark transfer from the dying patriarch to his chosen successor.
Stoicism during initiation is culturally mandatory; a single shed tear is acknowledged as a minor failure against the ideal.
The sacred oil of Marmola is an extraordinarily powerful substance even in tiny quantities; its existence is a state secret considered worth killing to conceal.
The Marmolans load cargo onto visiting ships by a secret method performed while visitors sleep after a feast; they would rather die than reveal the technique.
Ancient weapons from Terra Prima are revered above modern arms within Castakan warrior culture.
Castakan warriors are oath-bound to the Empire and regard treachery as contemptible.
An honorable death in battle is preferable to survival through surrender, according to the Castakan warrior code.
A titled rank of baron exists within the ruling hierarchy of Marmola and Castaka, subject to imperial oath and formal succession.
major_events: Tonto narrates the origin of the Metabaron caste to Lothar, establishing the volume's storytelling frame aboard the metabunker.
An Imperial Merchants Guild ship arrives at Marmola to collect marble for the Techno-Pope's temple-bank and inadvertently witnesses the Marmolans' secret sacred technology.
Othon's industrial accident traps him under rubble, forcing the Castakan elders to choose between secrecy and family loyalty.
The family council votes to save Othon; a glowing orb is used to levitate the stone block, exposing the sacred technology to imperial witnesses.
Baron Berard declares the discovery a major technical revolution, orders the witnesses killed, and names Othon the next baron.
Baron Berard duels Othon, deliberately accepts a wound to demonstrate sacrifice, then performs the spirit and birthmark transfer before dying.
Ten days after Berard's death, a multi-faction space war erupts over Marmola; the Imperial House wins and the Black Endoguard betrays one side.
The Castaka fortress is besieged; outnumbered defenders choose honorable death over surrender and the volume ends mid-battle.
open_uncertainties: The exact nature and properties of the sacred oil — its origin, how it is produced, and how it relates to the glowing orb used to levitate the stone block — are not explained in this volume.
The precise mechanism of the spirit and birthmark transfer is not described beyond that it is performed between elder and successor and leaves a physical mark.
The identity of the figure who uses the glowing orb and collapses is not explicitly confirmed.
The identity and function of the large faceted object suspended in a glowing sphere inside the metabunker are never explained.
Whether the Castakan warrior who crashes through the window at the volume's end survives, and the outcome of the last stand, are unresolved.
The exact content of the secret the Marmolans fear exposing to the Empire beyond involving the sacred oil and stone-loading method is not fully defined.
The nature of the substance called 'lupium' mentioned briefly during the rescue debate is unclear.
Several unnamed elders and attendants present at key council and duel scenes are never identified.
recurring_motifs: Hereditary bodily mutilation and cybernetic augmentation as warrior initiation: the father destroys the son's ear and part of the right brain, then replaces them with bionics.
Sacrifice and deliberate self-harm as the defining virtue of the Metabaron lineage.
Secrecy as survival: the sacred oil and the stone-loading method are protected at any cost, including killing witnesses.
Spirit and knowledge transferred physically from father to successor across generations, marked by a birthmark.
Stoicism and suppression of emotion enforced as warrior identity; even a single tear is noted as a minor failure.
Industrial labor (stone cutting) as a surface concealing sacred and dangerous hidden technology.
The tension between imperial loyalty and clan secrecy.
Honorable death in battle as preferable to survival through surrender or treachery.
title: The Stonecutters
